name: Multiple Agents Working Together
gist: Papers about coordinating several agents to solve problems together, like a team brainstorming or dividing tasks.
explain: Instead of one agent solving a problem alone, what if you had multiple agents with different strengths working as a team? One agent might be good at math, another at reading and summarizing, another at logical reasoning. They divide the work, pass information to each other, and combine their answers. This is inspired by how humans work in teams: you brainstorm together, point out flaws in each other's ideas, and build on what the group learns. The papers here explore how to coordinate multiple agents so they actually help each other instead of getting in the way.

The tricky part is making coordination actually work. Multiple agents mean more communication overhead — they have to pass messages, wait for each other, and resolve disagreements. If they are all calling the same tools, they might waste time on redundant calls. If they specializes but don't communicate well, they might end up solving different parts of the problem in isolation without realizing they contradict each other. And debugging a multi-agent system is much harder because failures can cascade in unpredictable ways. The system has more moving parts, more failure modes, and more places for things to go wrong.

Researchers work on agent collaboration frameworks that let teams of agents solve problems together. Some papers focus on communication protocols — how agents signal what they are doing and what they found out. Others focus on task division — making sure each agent gets a piece of the problem that plays to its strengths. Some look at voting or consensus mechanisms, where multiple agents independently tackle a subproblem and then combine their answers. The goal is to show that a team of agents can solve harder problems than any single agent could alone, but without the overhead drowning the benefits.

papers.title: AgentWebBench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Coordination in Agentic Web
papers.contribution: Multi-agent coordination lags centralized retrieval as expected but gap shrinks with model scale; decentralized access concentrates traffic, test-time scaling improves performance, and strong results require careful planning and sufficient interactions.

papers.title: Beyond Majority Voting: LLM Aggregation by Leveraging Higher-Order Information
papers.contribution: Both algorithms consistently outperform standard baselines on synthetic data, fine-tuning benchmarks like UltraFeedback and MMLU, and real-world healthcare settings.

papers.title: CORRECT: COndensed eRror RECognition via knowledge Transfer in multi-agent systems
papers.contribution: CORRECT improves step-level error localization by up to 19.8% over existing advances while operating at near-zero overhead, with the CORRECT-Error dataset providing 2,000+ annotated trajectories via error-injection pipeline.

papers.title: Distilling Task-Level Coordination Policies for Generalizable Multi-Agent Cooperation
papers.contribution: Achieves comparable success rates and execution efficiency to RL methods while generalizing to unseen team compositions and larger layouts without retraining, reducing inference overhead.

papers.title: EvoMAS: Heuristics in the Loop—Evolving Smarter Agentic Workflows
papers.contribution: EvoMAS consistently outperforms existing methods across multiple domains while maintaining cost efficiency, with roles evolving from homogeneous actors to specialized reasoning ensembles.

papers.title: Learning Efficient and Interpretable Multi-Agent Communication
papers.contribution: GLC outperforms state-of-the-art methods delivering superior task performance, higher communication efficiency, and enhanced human interpretability across multiple benchmarks.

papers.title: Learning to Share: Selective Memory for Efficient Parallel Agentic Systems
papers.contribution: Significantly reduces overall runtime while matching or improving task performance on AssistantBench and GAIA through learned memory admission.

papers.title: Scaling Small Agents Through Strategy Auctions
papers.contribution: SALE reduces reliance on largest agent by 52%, lowers overall cost by 35%, and improves pass@1 with negligible overhead, enabling effective small-agent scaling.

papers.title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems Against Corruptions via Node Contribution Backpropagation
papers.contribution: Notably outperforms existing multi-agent system defense mechanisms in complex and dynamic environments, providing effective guardrail for trustworthy multi-agent system deployment.

papers.title: Towards Sustainable Investment Policies Informed by Opponent Shaping
papers.contribution: Demonstrates theoretically why Advantage Alignment systematically favors socially beneficial equilibria by biasing learning dynamics toward cooperation, informing policy mechanisms to align market incentives with long-term sustainability.

papers.title: TreeCUA: Efficiently Scaling GUI Automation with Tree-Structured Verifiable Evolution
papers.contribution: TreeCUA-DPO improves GUI planning by leveraging branch information from adjacent trajectories, enabling efficient scaling of GUI automation with tree-structured verifiable evolution.

papers.title: A Diagnostic Study of Multi-Agent LLMs for Real-World Debates
papers.contribution: Process-level diagnostics align more closely with human judgments and reveal interaction failures that standard outcome-only measures overlook.

papers.title: A Two-Tier Perspective on Inference-Time Parallelism in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.contribution: TIPEX demonstrates complementary effects of parallelism levels across task complexities, with intermediate difficulty benefiting most from coordination.

papers.title: ATLAS: Constraints-Aware Multi-Agent Collaboration for Real-World Travel Planning
papers.contribution: ATLAS improves pass rate on TravelPlanner from 23.3% to 44.4% and achieves 84% on realistic travel tasks with live information, significantly outperforming ReAct (59%) and monolithic agents (27%).

papers.title: Agent Primitives: Reuseable Latent Building Blocks for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: Improves accuracy by 12.0-16.5% over single-agent baselines while reducing token usage and latency by 3×-4× compared to text-based MAS.

papers.title: AgentSteerTTS: A Multi-Agent Closed-Loop Framework for Composite-Instruction Text-to-Speech
papers.contribution: Consistent improvements on composite-instruction benchmark and public test sets for expressive control.

papers.title: AgentTailor: A Semantic-Aware LLM-Based Multi-Agent System with Actor-Critic Structure
papers.contribution: AgentTailor achieves 91.36% average accuracy on six datasets while reducing tokens by 21.2%–61.6% compared to baseline multi-agent systems.

papers.title: Ask Less, See More: Communication-Conditioned Token Pruning for Vehicle-to-Vehicle Cooperative Autonomous Driving with Multimodal Large Lang
papers.contribution: V2V-CCM achieves state-of-the-art performance on V2V-QA and V2V-GoT-QA while substantially reducing communication and inference costs compared to existing pruning methods.

papers.title: Beyond Correctness: Distance-Based Social Dynamics of Multi-Agent Debate
papers.contribution: The work shows structured, distance-dependent movements in solution space under social pressure, clarifying when interaction improves, stabilizes, or degrades quality.

papers.title: CARD: Towards Conditional Design of Multi-agent Topological Structures
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms static baselines on HumanEval, MATH, and MMLU with higher accuracy and robustness across diverse conditions.

papers.title: CVE-Factory: Scaling Expert-Level Agentic Tasks for Code Security Vulnerability
papers.contribution: Enables large-scale agentic task synthesis: fine-tuned Qwen3-32B improves from 5.3% to 35.8% on LiveCVEBench, surpassing Claude 4.5 Sonnet.

papers.title: ClinTutor-R1: Advancing Scalable and Robust One-to-Many Alignment in Clinical Socratic Education
papers.contribution: Outperforms base models by over 20% and achieves parity with reasoning models while maintaining scalability across expanding cohorts.

papers.title: Detecting Perspective Shifts in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: Demonstrates TDKPS detects changes that correlate sensitively, specifically, and significantly with real exogenous events, establishing the first principled framework for monitoring behavioral dynamics.

papers.title: EduMirror: Modeling Educational Social Dynamics with Value-driven Multi-agent Simulation
papers.contribution: EduMirror generates educational social dynamics that are realistic, theory-consistent, and measurable, enabling in silico hypothesis testing and counterfactual intervention analysis.

papers.title: Emergent Communication Under Misinformation
papers.contribution: Finds that risks of malign misrepresentation promote emergence of compositional languages; adaptability of malign intermediaries is crucial for consistent pressure toward compositionality.

papers.title: Emergent Coordination in Multi-Agent Language Models
papers.contribution: We show multi-agent LLM systems can be steered via prompt design from mere aggregates to higher-order collectives with identity-linked differentiation and goal-directed complementarity.

papers.title: EvoMAS: Evolutionary Generation of Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: EvoMAS consistently improves task performance over human-designed and prior automatic MAS generation methods, reaching 79.1% on SWE-Bench-Verified.

papers.title: GraphPlanner: Graph-Based Agentic Routing for LLMs
papers.contribution: Improves accuracy by up to 9.3% while reducing GPU cost from 186.26 GiB to 1.04 GiB; generalizes to unseen tasks with strong zero-shot capabilities.

papers.title: Great Minds Think Alike: Contextual Tacit Communication for Decentralized LLM-Agent Cooperation
papers.contribution: Improves cooperation performance over baselines while reducing runtime overhead compared with communication-based methods across VIKI, C-WAH, and TDW-MAT benchmarks.

papers.title: HieraMAS: Optimizing Intra-Node LLM Mixtures and Inter-Node Topology for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods on reasoning and coding benchmarks while achieving better cost-performance trade-offs.

papers.title: Judgment Operators: A Composition-Invariant Substrate for Multi-Agent Action Spaces
papers.contribution: Achieves 0% observed violation rate versus 48-68% baselines with composition-invariant enforcement and 13.5-20.5% cross-model transfer.

papers.title: LLawCo: Learning Laws of Cooperation for Modeling Embodied Multi-Agent Behavior
papers.contribution: Achieves 4.5% success rate improvement on PARTNR-Dialog and 6.8% on TDW-MAT benchmarks across multiple LLM backbones over state-of-the-art communicative agent frameworks.

papers.title: Latent Collaboration in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: Outperforms single agents and text-based MAS by up to 14.6% higher accuracy, reduces output token usage by 70.8%-83.7%, and provides 4-4.3× faster inference across math, science, and code generation benchmarks.

papers.title: Learning Decentralized LLM Collaboration with Multi-Agent Actor Critic
papers.contribution: CoLLM-CC outperforms Monte Carlo and CoLLM-DC on long-horizon and sparse-reward tasks, demonstrating when centralized vs decentralized critics benefit decentralized LLM collaboration.

papers.title: Learning Multi-Agent Coordination via Sheaf-ADMM
papers.contribution: Yields improved robustness to distribution shifts and higher solve rates compared to MPNNs on maze pathfinding, classification, and Sudoku.

papers.title: MAS$^2$: Self-Generative, Self-Configuring, Self-Rectifying Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: MAS² achieves performance gains up to 19.6% over state-of-the-art MAS on complex scenarios and superior cross-backbone generalization with up to 15.1% improvement on unseen LLMs.

papers.title: MOC: Multi-Order Communication in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: MOC consistently improves task performance and reduces communication costs across six diverse datasets and multiple LLM backbones.

papers.title: Mosaic: Runtime-Efficient Multi-Agent Embodied Planning
papers.contribution: Across AI2-THOR and search-and-rescue benchmarks, Mosaic achieves 27-32% faster execution, 30-33% fewer LLM calls, and 4-10% higher success rates.

papers.title: MulFCoder: Framework-conditioned Multi-agent for MLLM-based Multi-framework Front-end Code Generation
papers.contribution: Substantially improves compilation success rate and reduces framework-specific errors, with particularly pronounced gains on Angular.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Teams Hold Experts Back
papers.contribution: LLM teams consistently underperform their best member by up to 41.1% on ML benchmarks, with expert leveraging rather than identification identified as the primary bottleneck, though this consensus-seeking improves robustness to adversarial agents.

papers.title: Navigating the Energy Landscape of Collaboration: Multi-Agent Communication Graph Generation via Score-Based Diffusion
papers.contribution: MAGE achieves state-of-the-art performance on representative benchmarks, and qualitative analysis reveals that generated graphs mirror functional specialization of human organizations, validating the thermodynamic hypothesis.

papers.title: Opponent Shaping in LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Demonstrates LLM agents can guide opponents toward exploitable equilibria in competitive games and promote coordination in cooperative games, establishing opponent shaping as a key multi-agent dimension.

papers.title: RADAR: Redundancy-Aware Diffusion for Multi-Agent Communication Structure Generation
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines across six benchmarks with higher accuracy, lower token consumption, and greater robustness through redundancy-aware topology generation.

papers.title: Representational Similarity and Model Behavior in Multi-Agent Interaction
papers.contribution: Similar representation spaces drive higher cooperation but reduce novelty and creativity; similarity in early layers shows strongest association with these dynamics, suggesting shared lexical grounding as a key factor.

papers.title: Social Agents: Collective Intelligence Improves LLM Predictions
papers.contribution: Improves LLM predictions by up to 67.45% over single-LLM baselines across eleven behavioral prediction tasks through collective intelligence.

papers.title: Stop Wasting Your Tokens: Towards Efficient Runtime Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: SupervisorAgent reduces token consumption by average 29.68% without compromising success rate on GAIA benchmark.

papers.title: Systematic Failures in Collective Reasoning under Distributed Information in Multi-Agent LLMs
papers.contribution: A lightweight structured communication protocol substantially improves collective reasoning; findings identify actionable bottlenecks in multi-agent information exploration.

papers.title: TOM-SWE: User Mental Modeling For Software Engineering Agents
papers.contribution: ToM-SWE achieves 59.7% task success on stateful SWE-bench versus 18.1% for OpenHands, with 86% user satisfaction in a three-week study with professional developers.

papers.title: UIS-Digger: Towards Comprehensive Research Agent Systems for Real-world Unindexed Information Seeking
papers.contribution: Achieves 26.36% on UIS-QA benchmark with 30B backbone, outperforming systems integrating O3 and GPT-4.1 at revealing UIS limitations.

papers.title: Visual Multi-Agent System: Mitigating Hallucination Snowballing via Visual Flow
papers.contribution: ViF consistently reduces hallucination snowballing across eight benchmarks based on four common MAS structures and ten base models with lightweight, plug-and-play implementation.
